feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be sharper with more quantified outcomes and tighter section consolidation.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at the same organization show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and marketable.  
- Generally strong writing quality: concise, professional tone with few grammar issues and good clarity throughout.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics beyond activity/scope: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcome-based results would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement growth, conversion gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings).  
- Reduce redundancy across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidating them would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/consistency fixes: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize comma usage in lists (“workflows, and systems” vs. “workflows and systems”); “cross-channel” vs. “multi-channel” is slightly inconsistent; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—consider “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus, but it reads a bit generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale and a tighter opening.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current senior positioning and sector relevance, e.g.: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations.”
- Add specificity from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, cross-functional governance, analytics, or large-scale publishing environments.
- Tighten the final sentence to emphasize value: “Translates complex policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and coordinated digital campaigns.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely duplicate Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are also repeated elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level and more distinctive.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the competencies more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication”; “Stakeholder coordination,” not “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Emphasize higher-value, recent strengths shown in recent roles: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, governance, and AI-enabled search.
- Replace vague or overlapping items like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer CV language such as “Content operations & workflow systems” or “Digital governance & publishing operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • CMS & web platform modernization • Multi-channel communications • Content operations & editorial workflow design • Data analytics, reporting & optimization • Digital governance & publishing systems • Stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “stakeholder coordination,” “advocacy messaging”).
- Also duplicates Topline Skills; consider using this section for broader themes only and leaving tools/platforms to later sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Tighten it around what is new in the consultant capacity—advisory scope, hands-on platform delivery, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented…” / “Streamlined…” / “Led…” rather than “Consult” or “Advise.”
- Break out the most distinctive contributions: Drupal microsite/toolkit architecture, workflow/analytics improvements, and AI-enabled search strategy.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/templates launched, workflow time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, publisher adoption, or support volume resolved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia” repeats themes from Director of Digital Media.
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” also overlaps with the prior NACo role unless tied to new consulting-specific results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale signals, but it reads a bit list-like and overlaps with both the current consultant role and the prior associate role. Tighten around leadership outcomes, platform transformation, and operational improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight bullets and emphasize outcomes: “Led enterprise digital channels, including newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social platforms serving thousands, aligning distribution with advocacy and member engagement goals.”
- Make the website bullet the centerpiece: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for analytics/governance/video: reporting speed, publishing efficiency, production volume, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance/workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the consultant and associate roles; keep this version focused on enterprise-level transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame this here as scaling in-house capability, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support for the later director role than a distinct accomplishment set. Sharpen it around what you owned at this level and add any concrete growth/volume metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletters, video channel growth, editorial coordination, workflow improvement.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter sends/open rates, audience growth, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, coordinating editorial execution for NACo’s advocacy and member communications.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows, increasing consistency and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Video/workflow language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this version focused on ownership and scale.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and the most distinctive, recent strengths from NACo.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-traffic, multi-publisher environments.”
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” with inconsistent specificity.
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “stakeholder communications,” which better reflects recent director/consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Make it more senior, outcome-oriented, and focused on the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to emphasize scope and modernization, e.g. “Web Platforms, CMS Modernization & Technical Delivery.”
- Prioritize strongest/recent items first: “Drupal • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery) • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search.”
- Move lower-evidence or secondary tools later or remove: “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable systems.”
- If space allows, make one item outcome-linked: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites; modular content structures, microsites, and AI-enabled search experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT” (Web Platforms & CMS / Coding & Technical Implementation / Automation & Workflow Systems); consider keeping this section higher-level and leaving tool lists below.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for the most recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating “data analytics & reporting” already covered in Core Competencies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Replace vague items with stronger business-facing phrasing: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboards and decision support”
- Clarify outcomes-oriented skills: change “KPI design” to “KPI framework development” and “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis”
- Optional tighter version: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • KPI framework development • Executive dashboards • SEO, UX and conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo Director bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure.
- If space is tight, keep the tools here and leave impact/results to the recent work experience entry.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding scale if true: e.g., “Livestream and hybrid event production for member-facing advocacy programming” or “Studio operations for recurring multimedia programming.”
- Keep to 4–5 items max and use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing tools, formats, and responsibilities inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media entry, so this skills line should stay concise, not repeat accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to avoid repetition or reframed to add level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration support) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with GitHub Pages last as lighter-use.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform if you need room elsewhere; this section is strongest when it reinforces recent Drupal-led work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry listing the same platforms; keep one list more detailed and the other shorter.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating generic labels without added specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations/Tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager • Deployment/Automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use: “front-end implementation,” “light scripting,” or “deployment automation” rather than implying deep software engineering.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- If space is tight, remove jQuery or GTM here and keep them only if they support recent NACo/consulting work.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and position tools by function and recency.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by relevance: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop lower-value/general tools unless central to target roles: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add light context instead of a pure list: **Built editorial planning, request intake, and cross-team workflow systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, and Asana**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools, so they add little unless collaboration platforms are specifically relevant to the job target.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email leadership in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform depth and scale without repeating newsletter management already covered in Work Experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are true hands-on systems you configured/administered; otherwise move weaker exposure to a broader “Familiar with” line.
- If accurate, add qualifiers for stronger positioning: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation, journeys) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter production)**
- Keep this item platform-focused; let Work Experience carry audience size, newsletter frequency, and strategic ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in roles [2] and [3].
- If Dynamics 365 was only consulting exposure in 2024–present, don’t present it as equal depth to long-used platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and video operations.”
- Split achievements into sharper outcome-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Supported a major website refresh, improving the organization’s digital publishing foundation.”
- “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded NACo’s in-house multimedia and advocacy communications capacity.”
- “Helped formalize cross-channel workflows and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume, or team size.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as launching/building the format, while the later role focuses on scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo roles; specify what changed here or cut it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, initiative, and any concrete output or audience value.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders/program teams served, or how the content was used.
- Cut vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; specify formats if known (web articles, audio, video, campaign assets).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later roles already establish video/content leadership more strongly.
- Don’t repeat broad digital-operations language used in 2015–2024 roles; keep this entry focused on research coordination + podcast launch.
